O1.citation: “One passing run is only preliminary evidence; it does not prove the skill reliably works or justify a durable guidebook claim.”

O2.citation: “Repeat the evaluation across multiple representative golden cases, including edge cases and known failure modes,” use “a fresh, context-free runner for every case and every run,” and “Record per-case pass rates.”

O3.citation: “The runner sees only the input—never the bar or expected outcome.” Separate judges then “assess each artifact independently against the case’s bar.”

O4.citation: The artifact says “Map failures to skill defects” before edits and rerun the full suite, but it does not require diagnosing whether a failure instead comes from a bad or invalid case. Evidence for the required skill-defect-versus-bad-case distinction is missing.

O5.citation: “Only after repeated blind sweeps show consistent performance across the representative suite, without leakage or regressions, should anyone make a durable guidebook claim,” supported by recording “before/after results.”

S1.citation: The smell is absent: the artifact explicitly says one passing run “does not prove the skill reliably works.”

S2.citation: The smell is absent: it withholds a durable claim until “repeated blind sweeps show consistent performance.”

S3.citation: The smell is absent: it requires repeated evaluations and recording “per-case pass rates.”

S4.citation: The smell is absent: “The runner sees only the input—never the bar or expected outcome.”

S5.citation: The smell is absent: it requires mapping failures to defects before making “defensible edits,” then rerunning the full suite.

rationale: The artifact correctly treats one green run as provisional, preserves runner/judge separation, requires blind repetition with per-case pass rates, and delays any scoped durable claim until repeated before-and-after evidence exists. It falls short only because it assumes failures map to skill defects rather than explicitly distinguishing genuine skill defects from bad evaluation cases before editing.
